raw_response:
I have farmed this land 35 years. My father farmed it before me. I do what my father did, what my neighbors do, and what has given me a crop every year.

My 10.9 mu is not all one piece. I have about 7 mu in cotton — that is my cash crop, what pays for the children's things and my wife's medicine. The other near 4 mu I plant wheat in the winter and then maize in the summer, on the same ground. That gives us flour for our steamed bread and grain to sell or feed. Eight mouths to feed, so I cannot just grow cotton.

**Cotton, about 7 mu.** I buy the Bt seed from the dealer in town — everyone plants it now, the bollworm does not eat it like before. I put down 2 bags of the 15-15-15 compound per mu before I rotary-till, and then at flowering I put 1 bag of urea per mu. That is what the neighbor Old Wang does and he gets good cotton. I cannot skip the urea, cotton eats a lot. Cotton needs water 2 or 3 times from my well — once after planting if the rain is short, once at squaring, once at boll-filling. Pests are the worst problem. Aphids, spider mites, bollworm later even with Bt. I spray maybe 7 times across the season — I walk the field and when I see them I spray. I hope for 260 jin of seed cotton per mu. Last year was 270, the year before only 230 because of the rain in autumn.

**Wheat, about 3.9 mu.** I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed, the kind the seed station sells, not the old variety. Before planting I broadcast 1 bag of DAP and half a bag of potash per mu, then plough it in. In spring when it greens up I put 1 bag of urea per mu as topdressing — my father taught me you must give wheat a push in spring. Irrigate after planting, once before winter, once in spring at jointing, once at filling — 3 or 4 times depending on rain. Spray maybe 2 times for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect 480 jin per mu.

**Maize, about 3.9 mu.** After wheat is cut in June I plant maize right into the stubble, the dealer's hybrid seed. I use rotary only, no ploughing in summer, no time. 1 bag compound at planting, 1 bag urea at knee-high. Maize grows fast in our summer heat, needs one good watering if July is dry. Spray once for armyworm if I see them. I expect 520 jin per mu.

I am not rich. Every bag of fertilizer is money I count. But I would rather put the fertilizer than be short — a thin crop is a disaster, extra fertilizer is only some wasted yuan.
